text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's autotune landing we're seeing an intermittent p99 regression (~8-15%) on the 8GPU continuous-batching pool when the kernel selector flips to the `matmul_fused` path for long sequences. Looks correlated with bursty small-batch traffic that keeps triggering kernel launches. Suspect launch overhead + KV cache warmup compounding.

Sam: Can you paste the repro steps / minimal command? I can run local microbench.

Maya: repro I used:
```
./scripts/bench/pipeline_warmup.sh --model gptx-13b --gpus 8 --seq-len 1200 --qps 25 --duration 10m
```
Observed after ~3-5 min the selector starts preferring `matmul_fused` for >1024 and p99 climbs. Dumped a short perf capture below.

Raj: Perf snippet from the capture (samples aggregated):
```
PROFILE SUMMARY
window: 2026-03-15T14:22..14:28
avg_token_ms: 3.2
p99_token_ms: 45.1  (baseline before change: 41.8)
Kernel picks:
 - attention_split     62% tokens, avg 25.0ms
 - matmul_fused        30% tokens, avg 60.2ms (launch overhead ~8.1ms)
 - fallback_generic     8% tokens
KV cache warmup:
 - first-1k-token miss-rate: 42%
 - steady-state miss-rate: 3%
Queue stats:
 - mean batch size: 3.1
 - continuous-batch flush interval: ~10ms
```

Olivia: That launch overhead is suspicious — `matmul_fused` seems to have high startup cost that only amortizes on large batches. With a mean batch ~3 it's never amortized.

Tom: Two ideas:
1) Adjust autotune utility to include an amortization model: effective_ms = launch_ms / (expected_tokens_per_launch) + run_ms
2) Introduce a small "probe and pin" on kernel switch: before switching traffic, run N probe requests to measure real launch cost and KV miss behaviour.

Jen: Quick mitigation we could roll out today: increase sticky-kernel TTL from 30s -> 90s for pools with low average batch depth, and lower the aggressiveness of switching for seq_len thresholds in continuous-batch mode. That avoids flip-flopping during warmup.

Maya: I also noticed KV miss spikes line up with switches. When a new kernel path wins we rebuild per-gpu KV caches and that adds CPU/GPU work + memory pressure. Could try pre-warming caches on candidate kernels using a tiny synthetic prefix.

Raj: Sampled stack traces during launch — majority of the 8ms is kernel init + CUDA context ops, not model compute. So pre-warming or avoiding frequent switches seems like the right approach.

Maya: I've opened a tracking ticket: https://redwood.internal/INFR-2307 — notes + perf dumps attached. ci-bot: please add `eng-runtime` label and assign to the oncall.

ci-bot: Created ticket INFR-2307 and added label `eng-runtime`. :white_check_mark:

Sam: I'll take ownership of a microbenchmark and a small PR for the amortization model. Plan: add `--autotune-samples` probe flag and a config knob `autotune.min_amort_tokens=64` to avoid switching unless we expect enough tokens to amortize launch cost. I'll post results by EOD.

Olivia: Also worth adding a metric to Console: per-kernel launch_latency and kernel_switch_count per-pool so we can alert before p99 drifts. Small dashboard + alert.

Tom: For the medium-term: autotuner should be architecture-aware (we already have per-arch profiles) but also scheduling-aware. E.g. when scheduling sees sustained low queue depth, bias towards low-launch-overhead kernels.

Jen: For immediate canary, recommend: sticky-ttl=90s, min_amort_tokens=128, enable probe=on for canary pool only. Roll to canary for 2 hours and compare p50/p95/p99. I'll coordinate the rollout.

Maya: Sounds good. Assigning action items in the ticket: Sam -> microbench + PR, Jen -> canary rollout, Olivia -> console metrics, Raj -> root-cause trace. I'll follow up after canary.

Sam: On it. :rocket:

Olivia: Thanks — this explains the weird regression we were chasing yesterday. :+1:
